entries.title: Data augmentation using generative networks to identify dementia
entries.abstract: Data limitation is one of the most common issues in training machine learning classifiers for medical applications. Due to ethical concerns and data privacy, the number of people that can be recruited to such experiments is generally smaller than the number of participants contributing to non-healthcare datasets. Recent research showed that generative models can be used as an effective approach for data augmentation, which can ultimately help to train more robust classifiers sparse data domains. A number of studies proved that this data augmentation technique works for image and audio data sets. In this paper, we investigate the application of a similar approach to different types of speech and audio-based features extracted from interactions recorded with our automatic dementia detection system. Using two generative models we show how the generated synthesized samples can improve the performance of a DNN based classifier. The variational autoencoder increased the F-score of a four-way classifier distinguishing the typical patient groups seen in memory clinics from 58% to around 74%, a 16% improvement
entries.authors: Bahman Mirheidari, Yilin Pan, Daniel Blackburn, Ronan O'Malley, Traci Walker, Annalena Venneri, Markus Reuber, Heidi Christensen

entries.title: Differential Diagnosis of Frontotemporal Dementia and Alzheimer's Disease using Generative Adversarial Network
entries.abstract: Frontotemporal dementia and Alzheimer's disease are two common forms of dementia and are easily misdiagnosed as each other due to their similar pattern of clinical symptoms. Differentiating between the two dementia types is crucial for determining disease-specific intervention and treatment. Recent development of Deep-learning-based approaches in the field of medical image computing are delivering some of the best performance for many binary classification tasks, although its application in differential diagnosis, such as neuroimage-based differentiation for multiple types of dementia, has not been explored. In this study, a novel framework was proposed by using the Generative Adversarial Network technique to distinguish FTD, AD and normal control subjects, using volumetric features extracted at coarse-to-fine structural scales from Magnetic Resonance Imaging scans. Experiments of 10-folds cross-validation on 1,954 images achieved high accuracy. With the proposed framework, we have demonstrated that the combination of multi-scale structural features and synthetic data augmentation based on generative adversarial network can improve the performance of challenging tasks such as differentiating Dementia sub-types.
entries.authors: Da Ma, Donghuan Lu, Karteek Popuri, Mirza Faisal Beg

entries.title: Causal Time Series Modeling of Supraglacial Lake Evolution in Greenland under Distribution Shift
entries.abstract: Causal modeling offers a principled foundation for uncovering stable, invariant relationships in time-series data, thereby improving robustness and generalization under distribution shifts. Yet its potential is underutilized in spatiotemporal Earth observation, where models often depend on purely correlational features that fail to transfer across heterogeneous domains. We propose RIC-TSC, a regionally-informed causal time-series classification framework that embeds lag-aware causal discovery directly into sequence modeling, enabling both predictive accuracy and scientific interpretability. Using multi-modal satellite and reanalysis data-including Sentinel-1 microwave backscatter, Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 optical reflectance, and CARRA meteorological variables-we leverage Joint PCMCI+ (J-PCMCI+) to identify region-specific and invariant predictors of supraglacial lake evolution in Greenland. Causal graphs are estimated globally and per basin, with validated predictors and their time lags supplied to lightweight classifiers. On a balanced benchmark of 1000 manually labeled lakes from two contrasting melt seasons (2018-2019), causal models achieve up to 12.59% higher accuracy than correlation-based baselines under out-of-distribution evaluation. These results show that causal discovery is not only a means of feature selection but also a pathway to generalizable and mechanistically grounded models of dynamic Earth surface processes.
entries.authors: Emam Hossain, Muhammad Hasan Ferdous, Devon Dunmire, Aneesh Subramanian, Md Osman Gani

entries.title: Diffusion limits of cyclic finite-velocity random motions along vector fields
entries.abstract: We investigate diffusion approximations for a class of multivariate inhomogeneous finite-velocity random motions motivated by models of active particles. A particle alternates cyclically among prescribed velocity fields $V_1,\dots,V_p$ with random run times and evolves according to either a \emph{flight} dynamics, consisting of piecewise-linear motion, or a \emph{gliding} dynamics, in which the particle follows the corresponding velocity flow. Under a Kac-type scaling that couples vanishing run times with diverging particle speed, we prove weak convergence of both processes to multidimensional diffusions. It turns out that the order of successive cyclic motions affects the diffusion limit. In addition to the second-order term generated by fluctuations of the random run times, the limiting drift contains directional derivatives $DV_i[V_j]$ of the underlying vector fields. In Stratonovich form, part of this drift is expressed through their Lie brackets $[V_i,V_j]$. Thus, the generic non-commutativity of the microscopic motions survives the diffusive scaling and generates a macroscopic drift which depends on the cyclic order. The limiting drift also distinguishes the flight and gliding dynamics, despite their being driven by the same vector fields and run times. Several examples, including run-and-reverse motion and cyclic dynamics generated by multiple vector fields, illustrate how the cyclic switching protocol and the geometry of the underlying velocity fields shape the limiting diffusions.
entries.authors: Olga Aryasova, Ilya Pavlyukevich, Yusif Sualah

entries.title: Textual Response-Aware Guidance for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness of Vision-Language Models
entries.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong zero-shot generalization but remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Existing adversarial fine-tuning methods often use pre-trained model guidance to preserve image--text alignment while improving robustness. Our analysis of visual representation drift reveals complementary limitations of two representative forms of guidance. Matching visual features constrains all directions equally, providing broad coverage without semantic emphasis. Matching prediction distributions prioritizes semantically relevant directions, but remains limited by the candidate texts and prediction probabilities. These limitations can hinder preservation of pre-trained image--text relationships and degrade zero-shot performance. We therefore propose Textual Response-Aware Guidance (TRAG), which constrains visual representation drift using the pre-trained text encoder's responses to local variations in input embeddings. TRAG constructs anchor-level constraints from the response directions and magnitudes around semantic anchors, then aggregates them using pre-trained image--anchor relevance, yielding an image-adaptive constraint. Extensive experiments across architectures and tasks demonstrate state-of-the-art clean and robust performance. Further analysis shows that TRAG helps preserve pre-trained image--text relationships.
entries.authors: Yubo Cui, Xianchao Guan, Zheng Zhang

entries.title: Hamiltonian dynamics with nonconservative forces on extended phase space: An analytical mechanics derivation
entries.abstract: This note derives the full Hamiltonian equations of motion on extended phase space for nonconservative and/or nonautonomous dynamical systems, with particular attention given to the momentum coordinate and generalized force associated with time. Time reparameterization is also considered, clarifying when it does or does not preserve Hamiltonian structure. The analytical mechanics framework is used throughout, with all developments formulated in terms of arbitrary symplectic coordinates; the main developments are not predicated on a Lagrangian description.
entries.authors: Joseph T. A Peterson, Manoranjan Majji, John L. Junkins

entries.title: Alchemically Transferable Parameters for Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
entries.abstract: Machine-learned circuit parameters could remove one of the main bottlenecks of variational quantum eigensolvers: the classical optimization loop, with its typical barren plateaus, local minima, and costly energy and gradient evaluations, is replaced by a direct prediction. Prior work showed that machine-learning models paired with a structured circuit design can transfer across system size and structure within hydrogenic systems. The next step: Extending them to organic molecules would seem to require re-training on use-case-specific training sets. In this work, we show that this is not necessary by establishing an alchemical approach. A geometric projection places surrogate hydrogen atoms along the bond directions of the target molecule and so maps its local bonding environment onto small hydrogenic fragments. Existing hydrogenic solvers can then be reused as they are. The only new quantity is a single projection radius per bond type, which is fitted once on a small reference molecule and reused unchanged thereafter. We demonstrate the approach on the separable-pair circuit designs that have been used in prior work and extend the approach to multi-circuit approaches that span effective bases for quantum subspaces.
entries.authors: Jonas Motyl, Jakob S. Kottmann

entries.title: Geometry and Stochastic Analysis of Flow and Diffusion Models: A Survey
entries.abstract: Flow-based and diffusion-based models have become the principal means of learning and sampling high-dimensional probability distributions, from images and video to proteins, molecules and physical fields, and increasingly language. Each carries a simple law to the law of the data along a curve of probability measures, and behind the variety of their names lie three geometries, those of the state space on which the data live, of the space of probability measures through which the curve passes, and of the space of paths traced by the generating process. A single analytic idea runs through the subject. Every score identity used to train a diffusion model is an integration by parts, on the noise, on the data or on Wiener space, and Malliavin calculus extends this to nonlinear and infinite-dimensional diffusions. We develop these foundations with full definitions and follow them through normalising flows, flow matching and few-step maps, diffusion models and their convergence theory, conditioning, Schr\"odinger bridges and stochastic control, and their extension to manifolds, Lie groups, discrete and function spaces and jump processes. We close with statistical physics, renormalisation and, more speculatively, holography, in which the radial direction of anti-de Sitter space can play the role of flow time. A table of the main methods and a collection of open problems complete the survey.
entries.authors: Ehsan Mirafzali, Razvan Marinescu

entries.title: Pooling ETAS triggering parameters across subduction margins: forecast transfer, estimator stability and sequence-limited skill in Mexico
entries.abstract: Pooling earthquake-triggering parameters can reduce estimation variability on margins with few recorded sequences, but its forecast value must be distinguished from the stability of simply freezing a fitted law. We fit the ETAS model to the Mexican national catalog above magnitude 5.0, using the Slab2 coverage mask as the domain. On a 4.7-year holdout the model gains 1.45 bits per earthquake over a time-independent spatial Poisson reference (cluster-resampled interval [-0.03, +2.75] bits), with two clusters carrying 90% of the signed gain. Using the Global CMT catalog we fit eight disjoint subduction margins and a joint model on 3,210 earthquakes sharing six triggering parameters with a background rate per margin; BIC favors the joint model by 184 units, though a parametric bootstrap rejects its exact shared specification. Transferred into Mexico with the local background fixed, six of seven foreign triggering sets score within 0.07 nats per event of the home fit. In leave-one-margin-out evaluation, the excluded-pool law's event-weighted paired gain is +0.0334 [+0.0002, +0.0670] nats per event; its lower limit sits barely above zero and crosses zero under alternative cluster-linking rules, so we read it as neither conclusive superiority nor guaranteed noninferiority. Across 28 overlapping annual evaluations, local refitting minus a pooled law frozen before the first origin has mean gain -2.07 nats/year (moving-block interval [-6.92, +1.15]), while local productivity varies by a factor of 5.4. Coverage of these intervals is unmeasured, and a measured analogue fell short of nominal; the paired median contrast's significance depends on a Gutenberg-Richter slope that is conventional rather than measured. These results support pooling as a regularized alternative to local fitting, short of equivalence, a universal law, or an optimal update policy.
entries.authors: Ricardo Mansilla S\'anchez, Ricardo Mansilla

entries.title: Applicability of a Thermodynamic Model to Rich-Hydrogen Flammability Assessment in SMR Containments
entries.abstract: Hydrogen combustion remains a critical safety concern during severe accidents in small modular reactors (SMRs). The compact containment can develop rich-hydrogen atmospheres through zirconium oxidation while oxygen gradually accumulates via radiolysis. Conventional flammability assessment methodologies, however, have been validated and applied only for lean-hydrogen atmospheres. This study establishes a thermodynamic flammability assessment method for rich-hydrogen conditions using the Calculated Adiabatic Flame Temperature (CAFT). In rich mixtures the deficient reactant becomes oxygen and the Lewis number exceeds unity, matching the hydrocarbon regime where CAFT is established. The CAFT was evaluated at 21 points along the measured upper flammability limit boundary of the U.S. NRC FITS database. The limit temperature remains quasi-constant within 17% across steam fractions of 5-50%. Its minimum value of 1112.5 K was adopted as a conservative threshold. The criterion was applied to the NuScale severe accident scenario LCC-05T-03. A transient flammable window is identified during the 44-48 hour interval, when 8-10% oxygen coexists with vigorous hydrogen generation and low steam fractions. These results show that the oxygen criterion alone cannot resolve transient flammability windows. The CAFT criterion enables more comprehensive flammability assessment for SMR containments.
entries.authors: Sihyeong Yu, Dosu Park, Jeesuk Shin, Joongoo Jeon

entries.title: First-passage tests of anomalous transport closures in heterogeneous aquifers
entries.abstract: Breakthrough curves (BTCs) record arrival times, but anomalous transport models are often fitted with time-normalized spatial concentration profiles. Here, the effect of this mismatch on groundwater-transport upscaling is tested. Analytical limits and high-$q$ scaling were verified first. Six first-passage models were then fitted to particle arrivals from 36 two-dimensional digital aquifer runs. The set included exact ADE, $q$ and time-memory extensions, a joint memory-$q$ model, Gamma-CTRW, and a two-path inverse-Gaussian mixture. After the operator was corrected, memory-qFPT was not selected in any run. AICc selected the two-path model in 20 runs, Gamma-CTRW in 15, and q-FPT in one. Median downstream holdout log-RMSE was 0.904, 0.914, and 0.959 for the two-path, Gamma-CTRW, and memory-qFPT models, respectively. The memory-$q$ parameters also failed an independent plume-scaling test ($R^2=0.189$; slope $=-0.332$). Meanwhile, multimodal downstream BTCs increased from 0\% in homogeneous media to 100\% in the strongest heterogeneity class. Gamma-CTRW was also favored in an independent synthetic field. Observation consistency is therefore necessary but not sufficient for physical validation. In these simulations, pathway and waiting-time structure was supported more strongly than a unique memory-$q$ law.
entries.authors: Ke-Ming Shen, Yi-Xuan Liu

entries.title: D-TINs for Track-Sampled Ice Sheet Surface Reconstruction from Satellite Altimetry Data
entries.abstract: Satellite altimetry samples ice sheets densely along tracks but sparsely across tracks, with frequent gaps in spatial coverage. We study the impact of this irregular support on surface reconstruction and introduce a new method, D-TIN, that applies Delaunay triangulation and barycentric interpolation directly to observed locations. A spatial holdout removes contiguous track intervals and nearby same-pass observations. We compare D-TIN with two common workflows, kriging and tile-based polynomial interpolation, to evaluate its accuracy and computational efficiency. Across seven ICESat-1 campaigns, D-TIN reduces RMSE by 12.1 m to 23.6 m relative to independent 5 km tile and polynomial based reconstruction. Its aggregate accuracy is close to the ordinary kriging workflow using a 1 km grid on the commonly used GStatSim platform while its median runtime is 252 times lower. A fixed-weight multiscale extension of D-TIN, called MS-D-TIN, gives the lowest aggregate RMSE, 67.5 m, while retaining the low computational cost of the D-TIN family.
entries.authors: Xiaoyu Xia, Noah Bergam, Abani Patra

entries.title: An Idealized Model of Buoyant Gas Spreading and Silt Release beneath Rough Cave Ceilings
entries.abstract: Gas exhaled by open-circuit divers collects under the ceilings of submerged caves, migrates along the rock, and dislodges loose silt that then falls through the passage, a process that cave divers call percolation. This study develops an idealized model of the process. Buoyant gas under a self-affine rough ceiling is treated as a quasi-static sequence of pools that fill to their spill points, release gas that climbs to the next high point, and merge where their levels meet. Moving contact lines strip silt from the rock, and the released silt settles as a spectrum of grain sizes that reduces the distance at which a diver can see. The computation agrees exactly with an independent depression-filling algorithm, conserves gas volume to round-off, and reproduces the known exponents of invasion percolation in its capillary limit. A balance between the relief of the ceiling and its dip defines a pool scale that organizes where gas collects, and the area covered by gas from a single source grows more slowly than the volume supplied, as predicted by the self-affine geometry. The cutoff at the pool scale is soft, so large pools persist on steeper ceilings than the scale alone would suggest. In a reference passage, the lead diver of a team releases far more silt than the diver behind, and a team releases far less than the sum of its members acting alone, because the lead diver fills the pools and strips the paths that later divers reuse. This ordering holds across every detachment efficiency and ceiling geometry tested. Visibility toward the exit at eye level continues to decline for an hour or more after a team has passed, as fine silt descends from a nearly opaque layer beneath the ceiling. Absolute silt masses and sighting ranges depend on quantities that have not been measured in caves, and the results are best read as scaling relations and comparisons between scenarios.
entries.authors: Sandy Hardian Susanto Herho, Dasapta Erwin Irawan, Rusmawan Suwarman, Deny Juanda Puradimaja

entries.title: EoSAlign: An Open-Source Software for Calculating, Comparing, and Aligning Pressure Under Extreme Conditions
entries.abstract: Accurate pressure determination is essential in high pressure experiments. Inconsistencies among pressure scales limit direct comparisons and contribute to uncertainty in measured properties, such as, phase boundaries, melting conditions, and thermodynamic models, especially above 100 GPa where existing scales diverge by >10 GPa. EoSAlign, an open-source software, can calculate, compare, and align pressures using a range of published calibrations. EoSAlign calculates pressure from experimental measurements (such as volume (A^3), Raman shift (cm^-1), or luminescence peak position (nm)) and it can be used to compare pressure values from different pressure standards. Using EoSAlign, we fit and align the bridgmanite and post-perovskite equations of state to a common scale, enabling us to reduce pressure scale related differences. EoSAlign can be applied to any high pressure data analysis to compare experimental results, improve consistency between studies, and advance our understanding of planetary interiors and high pressure physics.
entries.authors: Allison Pease, Heidi N. Krauss, Kassandra Amezcua, Sang-Heon Shim

entries.title: Bayesian Retrieval of L-Band Absorption by Ice using SMOS Brightness Temperatures over the Antarctic Plateau
entries.abstract: The low absorption of microwaves at L-band in ice enables the retrieval of internal ice sheet parameters from satellite observations. However, knowing the precise value of the ice absorption $\kappa$a(T ) as a function of temperature is a strict prerequisite. The existing knowledge is well constrained above 2 GHz and under 200 MHz, lacking constraints in the P-and L-bands. In this study, we infer ice absorption values using the spatial variations of L-band radiometric observations across Antarctica and comparing them with internal ice temperature variations through a simple emission model. More importantly, we adopt a probabilistic approach to determine a credible interval for absorption, using a Bayesian retrieval method. Our algorithm seeks the optimal multiplier factor $\alpha$ to apply to the current lowest estimate ice absorption formulation $\kappa$a(T ) proposed by M{\"a}tzler 2006, and computes the probability distribution of $\alpha$. The results show the absorption is most likely 1.5 to 1.7 times higher than this lowest formulation, which reduces the actual sensing depth at L-band.
entries.authors: Hippolyte Signargout (UGA), Ghislain Picard (UGA), Olivier Zahm (UGA), Ange Haddjeri (UGA), Marion Leduc-Leballeur (IFAC), Pierre Zeiger (UGA), Marco Brogioni (IFAC), Giovanni Macelloni (IFAC)

entries.title: AFNO: Universal Certifiably-Arbitrage-Free Operator Learning Framework for European Call-Price Surfaces
entries.abstract:
Neural operators (NOs) have been introduced as deep learning-powered solutions to the computational bottleneck of solving families of problems. Once trained, an NO can rapidly output approximate solutions, avoiding the need to rerun classical solvers. However, standard NO architectures cannot guarantee static no-arbitrage when predicting European call-price surfaces from market or model features and, as we verify experimentally, can yield negative PnL in downstream trading tasks.
  We introduce a certifiably arbitrage-free (AF) and universal encoder-decoder NO framework, continuously mapping inputs from a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) $\mathcal{H}$ over any fixed subset of $[0,\infty)^2$ to a convex combination of arbitrage-free European call-price surfaces by continuously solving an approximate nearest-neighbour problem. We show that a nearest arbitrage-free correction of an unconstrained predicted surface need not exist, implying that no-arbitrage cannot, in general, be restored through post-processing. Further, we show that standard NOs, such as the FNO and certain encoder-decoder NOs, admit parameter configurations whose outputs violate static no-arbitrage. Thus, out-of-the-box NOs generally cannot be certifiably restricted to arbitrage-free configurations, but may only be guided towards them through PINN-type regularization during training.
entries.authors: Anastasis Kratsios, Yannick Limmer, Hans Buehler, Blanka Horvath, Raeid Saqur

entries.title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding
entries.abstract: Recent advancements in multimodal diffusion language models (MDLMs) have exhibited strong global modeling capabilities through iterative refinement. We observe that mask uncertainty follows an overall downward trend during iterative denoising, while a few denoising steps exhibit localized entropy spikes closely associated with hallucinations. We argue that anomalous steps can be identified by measuring the entropy deviation of each denoising step from its neighboring temporal window. We hypothesize that discrete token commitment discards the distributional information at masked positions, limiting the continued interaction between candidate semantics and the context during entropy spikes. With this goal, we present StepRefine, a plug-and-play decoding strategy that leverages semantic context to achieve reliable denoising. The core of our method lies in a step-aware switch between discrete denoising and latent refinement. The model employs probability-weighted embeddings at entropy spike steps to preserve diverse reasoning hypotheses and performs multiple rounds of continuous refinement. Meanwhile, a refinement controller monitors distributional stability to reduce unnecessary loops and switch the model back to standard discrete denoising. Through extensive experiments, StepRefine demonstrates significant hallucination mitigation across different MDLMs on multimodal benchmarks.
entries.authors: Zhongxing Xu, Zhonghua Wang, Zhe Qian, Shiyan Su, Ming Hu, Xiaocheng Zou, Wei Feng, Mingquan Lin, Yuyin Zhou, Yifan Peng, Hamid Rezatofighi, Zongyuan Ge

entries.title: SELD: Detecting Silent Evidence Loss in Context Compression beyond the Answer
entries.abstract: Context compression is now routine for language models with long inputs, but a compressed context is useful only if it keeps the evidence for the answer. Existing checks compare the reader model's answer or its most likely words, and thus miss a frequent failure, silent evidence loss: key evidence is removed while the answer stays the same, leaving the answer unsupported and risky for other models that reuse the context. To address this challenge, we propose SELD (Silent Evidence Loss Detector), which needs no training and no labels. Its principle is that when evidence is lost, a reader model's preferences among the answers it leaves unsaid shift even if its answer does not, so comparing these preferences before and after compression reveals losses that answer checks cannot see. We also build SEL-Pairs, a benchmark of length-matched evidence and control deletions from three question-answering datasets. Quantitative and qualitative experiments with five reader models on it show that SELD consistently outperforms strong and recent baselines across compressors, compression rates and models, identifying the evidence-removing edit in 83% of matched pairs with unchanged answers, against 70% for the strongest baseline. These results show that evidence loss in compressed contexts can be detected even when the answer is unchanged.
entries.authors: Wentao Lei, Li Liu

entries.title: Actionable Feedback: Improving Model Capabilities from User Edit Data on Clinical Documentation
entries.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being deployed in clinical documentation workflows, where clinicians review and edit their outputs before use. In principle, these clinician edits represent a scalable source of supervision for model training. In practice, not all edits represent actionable feedback: for instance, on data drawn from real-world deployment of an AI clinical documentation product, our review suggests that over 45% of edited outputs contain user-added information that is not directly supported by the inputs to the model. Naively fine-tuning on such edits risks teaching the model to hallucinate. In this paper, we develop a method to address this challenge. Given that real clinician edits on deployed documentation tools are not publicly available, we first develop a taxonomy of clinician-editing behaviors, informed by data from a deployed AI clinical documentation product. Then, we develop a method for generating semi-synthetic clinician-edit data, informed by our taxonomy, on a discharge-summary generation task based on MIMIC-III, a public dataset. Finally, we introduce simple filtering methods for identifying actionable edits, with accuracy evaluated by expert review. We show empirically, on our semi-synthetic dataset, that naive fine-tuning on raw edited output increases ungrounded content, while our approach of progressively filtering toward grounded edits enables improvement on clinician-alignment metrics while retaining faithfulness to the input context.
entries.authors: Daniel P. Jeong, Yewon Byun, John Giorgi, Peng Xu, Zachary C. Lipton, Michael Oberst

entries.title: Development of a Long-Term Stable Three-Axis Single-Beam Vector Optically Pumped Magnetometer Using a Buffer-Gas-Free Rubidium Vapor Cell and Direct Absorption Frequency Locking for Unshielded Geomagnetic Monitoring
entries.abstract: Optically pumped magnetometers (OPMs) achieve ultra-high sensitivity, yet sustaining long-term stability in unshielded, dynamic geomagnetic environments remains challenging. Here, we present the design and unshielded validation of a three-axis vector OPM achieving sub-nanotesla accuracy using an off-the-shelf rubidium (Rb) ampoule and a vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL). Unlike conventional sensors, this system operates without high-pressure buffer gases, mitigating wall-collision relaxation via a single-beam geometry combined with active zero-field nulling and adiabatic 70 kHz AC heating. To suppress VCSEL thermal wavelength drift without sub-Doppler optics, active frequency stabilization based on direct absorption spectroscopy (DAS) was implemented across a wide capture range. Continuous evaluation in an unshielded laboratory in Okayama against synthetic geomagnetic records from the Kakioka and Kanoya observatories demonstrated exceptional horizontal tracking fidelity. Concurrently, the vertical transfer matrix resolved the regional geomagnetic coast effect, extracting Parkinson induction vectors reflecting regional conductivity contrast, with high robustness against DC electric railway interference. Spectral characterization showed an intrinsic white noise floor of 10-20 pT above 1 Hz, enhanced by digital oversampling beyond the 12-bit DAC quantization limit, while residual overlapped Allan deviation revealed a 0.1 nT bias instability at 100-200 s integration times. These results prove that a compact, low-cost OPM platform based on commercial components can suppress long-term drift and serve as a reliable instrument for geophysical surveys and unshielded magnetic sensing.
entries.authors: Minaru Kawamura

entries.title: Brasilidade: Measuring Brazilian Identity for Large Language Models
entries.abstract: This work presents a new benchmark that aims to address the limitations of current methods for evaluating LLMs in Brazilian Portuguese. We introduced Brasilidade, an assessment methodology comprised of standardized tasks distributed across four different domains, and we are making available the tasks from its first domain, which address nuances of the language, grammar, and variations of Brazilian Portuguese. The results show that model size, by itself, does not determine performance; several medium-sized models outperformed larger models in the protocols evaluated. Specific models for Portuguese, in general, did not perform above average, despite their targeted training. Different task levels revealed significant nuances: while some tasks proved easy for most models, others posed extreme challenges, and some yielded mixed results, with wide variations in performance. This clearly illustrates the need for benchmarks that address the limitations of the models in Brazilian Portuguese, allowing future training cycles to seek to overcome them. Project repository https://github.com/soberania-oficial/brasilidade
entries.authors: Jos\'e Roberto Homeli da Silva, Felipe Jorge do Nascimento, Lucas Coutinho Freitas, William Alberto Cruz Casta\~neda, Marcellus Amadeus

entries.title: Generative Learning on Manifolds for Probabilistic Seismic Performance Assessment and Structural Identifiability
entries.abstract: Seismic performance assessment relies on computationally expensive nonlinear simulations, limiting uncertainty quantification and inference of structural properties from observed responses. We develop a manifold-based generative framework that learns the joint distribution of uncertain structural parameters and seismic-response trajectories from limited high-fidelity simulations. Combining Diffusion Maps, score-based Diffusion Modeling, and Geometric Harmonics, the framework enables both forward probabilistic prediction and inverse inference. Applied to a nine-story steel moment-resisting frame, the results reveal which structural properties are identifiable from seismic performance and how uncertainty in these properties influences response. In particular, the learned representation captures post-capping degradation characteristics more effectively than individual strength parameters. Inverse inference identifies distinct structural configurations that produce similar seismic performance, with representative solutions independently validated using nonlinear simulations. These findings demonstrate how generative learning can support uncertainty-aware seismic assessment while revealing structural non-identifiability and alternative mechanisms underlying observed performance
entries.authors: Dimitris G Giovanis, Ioannis G Kevrekidis, Roger G Ghanem

entries.title: Landfalling tropical cyclones perturb Earth's rotation
entries.abstract: Natural disasters that devastate human societies can also alter Earth's rotation. The 2011 $M_w$ 9.1 T\={o}hoku earthquake, one of the most powerful earthquakes ever recorded, shortened the day by 1.80 microseconds. Tropical cyclones are the costliest weather disasters, yet whether they can alter Earth's rotation remains unknown. Here we use atmospheric reanalysis to estimate, and numerical simulations to confirm, that a landfalling tropical cyclone can transiently alter the length of day by amounts rivalling those by great earthquakes. For example, Hurricanes Harvey (2017) and Katrina (2005) lengthened the day by 1.87 microseconds and 2.29 microseconds, respectively. As the climate warms, tropical cyclones may become an increasingly important source of variability in Earth's rotation.
entries.authors: Yaxuan Yang, Lei Liu, Zhouyu Zhang, Yongjie Liu, Qingyuan Wang, Lin Li

entries.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Predict Atomic Oxygen Erosion of Polymers in Low Earth Orbit
entries.abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO), home to most active satellites, is projected to undergo a debris-fragmentation cascade known as Kessler Syndrome. In light of this eventuality, it is imperative to maximize the operational lifetime of LEO satellites. Instrumental to this goal is the development of next-generation polymeric materials with improved resistance to atomic oxygen (AO) erosion. Because genuine LEO exposure experiments are prohibitively expensive and LEO conditions are difficult to reproduce in the laboratory, data-driven approaches offer a promising alternative for accelerating materials discovery. Here, we develop a fine-tuned large language model (LLM) based on OpenAI's GPT-4o to predict the AO erosion yield ($E_y$) of polymers using a curated dataset of 201 measurements compiled from multiple NASA LEO exposure missions. The model achieves an order of magnitude error (OME) of 0.154 and a log-scaled coefficient of determination (log-$R^2$) of 0.719, outperforming conventional machine learning approaches while eliminating the need for extensive feature engineering. Notably, incorporating macroscopic descriptors such as film thickness and layering did not improve predictive performance, suggesting that AO erosion is governed primarily by chemical and environmental variables rather than bulk structural characteristics. This finding underscores the importance of chemically informed polymer design in developing materials with improved AO resistance, while demonstrating the ability of modern LLMs to effectively extract chemically meaningful relationships even when data is limited. Beyond its predictive accuracy, the proposed framework provides a scalable platform for rapidly screening candidate polymers, reducing reliance on costly spaceflight experiments.
entries.authors: Jared Solovei, Sakshi Agarwal, Aubrey Toland, Jeffrey G. Ethier, Vikas Varshney, Lisa M. Hall, Wolfgang Windl, Rampi Ramprasad

entries.title: M\"obius Interaction Filtering: Order-Selective Spectral Regularization for Multimodal Humor Detection
entries.abstract: Multimodal humor detection requires interpreting language, vocal delivery, and visual behavior jointly. Expressive fusion must also regulate how interactions of different orders enter the final judgment. We propose M\"obius Interaction Filtering (MoIF), which learns a modality-subset prediction function and imposes order-selective spectral regularization through its aggregation structure. Private temporal encoders and balanced reciprocal interaction construct supervised unimodal, bimodal, and trimodal predictors. Their uniform aggregate is exactly a M\"obius-domain filter with a geometrically decreasing interaction-order response. This formulation retains higher-order representations while regulating their contribution to prediction. Controlled UR-FUNNY perturbations reveal a pronounced decline in label-aligned signal-to-noise ratio across interaction orders. The induced filter improves the final ratio by 1.62-2.79 times relative to the co-trained trimodal predictor while preserving its own clean class-aligned signal under perturbation. Five-seed experiments achieve 70.6% accuracy and weighted F1 on UR-FUNNY, exceeding thirteen reproduced methods on these detection metrics. CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI evaluations establish applicability to sentiment prediction, and cross-seed analyses show more stable estimates on all three datasets. MoIF connects the organization of multimodal interactions to their statistical reliability through an executable spectral constraint. Code is available at https://github.com/D-ST-Sword/MoIF.
entries.authors: Jiahao Qin, Yiwen Wang

entries.title: Trace element distribution in coarse-grained Ca-Al-rich inclusions by femtosecond LA-ICP-MS: Implications for U-Pb chronology
entries.abstract: Calcium-aluminium-rich inclusions (CAIs) in chondrites are the first solids that formed in the Solar System, as established by U-Pb chronology. After initial condensation, coarse-grained CAIs experienced melting, resulting in igneous partitioning and spatial redistribution of trace elements among constituent minerals. Understanding these distributions is essential for identifying trace-element host phases and interpreting U-Pb ages. Rare earth elements (REEs) and the actinides Th and U are particularly informative tracers, yet actinide behavior in coarse-grained CAIs remains poorly constrained. Here, we present major- and trace-element distribution maps of six coarse-grained CAIs from CV3 (Vigarano-type) chondrites acquired by femtosecond laser ablation ICP-MS. In CAIs lacking perovskite or hibonite, our results show that Al,Ti-pyroxene is the dominant host of U, Th, and most REEs, with strong enrichments observed toward pyroxene grain edges, whereas light REEs reside in melilite. Trace-element zonation reflects igneous fractional crystallization and is overprinted by melt evaporation, which caused depletion of the most volatile REEs (Yb, Eu, Ce) and U in CAI outer regions and rims. Using Nd and Th distribution maps as proxies for Cm, we model the effects of 247Cm-235U decay on mineral-scale U isotopic compositions. Variable Cm-U partitioning among coexisting minerals is predicted to generate resolvable inter-mineral 235U/238U variations, with the largest excesses in melilite. These variations can produce apparent U-Pb age offsets of ~0.1-1.0 Myr when U isotopic compositions and radiogenic Pb are derived from isotopically distinct mineral reservoirs, but generally remain small (< 0.15 Myr) when using bulk U isotopic compositions. Our results demonstrate that fractional crystallization and melt evaporation exert a primary control on U distribution and isotope systematics in igneous CAIs.
entries.authors: Merel E. Onderwater, Elishevah M. M. E. van Kooten, Glenn J. MacPherson, Alexander N. Krot, Martin Bizzarro

entries.title: PyOTIS: an open-source Python package for stream solute transport with transient storage
entries.abstract: OTIS and OTIS-P provide transient-storage transport and parameter estimation, whereas E-OTIS adds coupled water-quality reactions in a separate MATLAB implementation. PyOTIS brings these workflows into an open-source Python package with legacy OTIS input support. Its contribution is software integration: a scriptable interface, structured simulation outputs, Jacobian-based parameter uncertainty, sensitivity analysis, and selectable transport schemes. A browser-based graphical user interface (GUI) provides example loading, custom parameter entry, breakthrough-curve and storage-zone plots, reference overlays, and calibration of supplied cases with confidence intervals. The package retains the OTIS Crank--Nicolson formulation and the E-OTIS reaction network; these are inherited model components rather than new process formulations. Evaluation distinguishes code comparisons, analytical convergence, and fits to observations. For the six OTIS manual examples, the comparisons distinguish model outputs from field observations and include agreement to seven significant figures for the steady-state iron profile. The nine-species E-OTIS comparison reports maximum absolute differences of order $10^{-14}$\,mg\,L$^{-1}$ against MATLAB. The conservative analytical benchmark shows approximately second-order convergence. For Clackamas River calibration, residual sums of squares differ from OTIS-P by 3.65--5.12\%, although individual parameter estimates differ by up to 39.1\%. These results support implementation consistency for the tested cases without establishing unique parameter estimates or validating every reaction pathway. Source code, example inputs, and verification scripts accompany the package.
entries.authors: Xuchen Ying, Binbin Wang

entries.title: First results from a borehole network for the seismic characterization of the Einstein Telescope Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site
entries.abstract: The low-frequency sensitivity of the Einstein Telescope depends on the seismic environment of its site, both through the mechanical coupling of ground motion to the test masses and through Newtonian noise. We present the first results of the seismic characterization of the Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site based on a network of recently instrumented boreholes covering the first seven months of 2026 at four underground stations and their co-located surface sensors. Two of these boreholes were deliberately sited next to railway infrastructure, so that the levels reported here describe how anthropogenic transients propagate to depth at different distances from the source. The analysis was carried out with \texttt{SiteChar}, a Python framework developed for this work to provide a common processing pipeline across different sensors, networks and observation periods. It processes the data in sequential chunks and separates the noise floor from the contribution of transients. We present a characterization of the catalogue of observed transients and a tentative classification. These measurements form part of an integrated site characterization approach that combines the observed seismic field with three-dimensional geological and wave-propagation models to predict Newtonian noise and ultimately guide its mitigation at the Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site.
entries.authors: L. D'Onofrio, S. Koley, P. Barneo, S. Bentvelsen, S. Danilishin, G. Degrande, S. Francois, S. Kadmiel, M. Kiehn, H. Michel, F. Nguyen, T. Niggemann, N. Nippe, J. Pretz, V. Tempel, B. Vink, W. Walk

entries.title: IntentTwin: Deconfounding Candidate Support and the Oracle-to-Deployment Gap in Offline Web Behavior Prediction
entries.abstract: Offline web-behavior benchmarks frequently insert the demonstrated action into a finite candidate set and then measure reranking. We show that this protocol can create a candidate-support confound: when the target is outside training support while all distractors are sampled from that support, support membership identifies the gold action without modeling behavior. We formalize this effect with support-identifiability rate (SIR), construct support-balanced candidate sets, and evaluate a target-free dual-path proposer that combines support retrieval with open-vocabulary DOM/LM proposals. On filtered OPeRA (4,282/469/992 train/dev/test steps), the original protocol has SIR 1.0000 on target-OOV rows and a support-only rule reaches 1.0000 OOV Exact@1. Support balancing reduces SIR to 0.0000; the strongest conditional reranker obtains 0.7214 overall Exact@1, 0.7988 on IV rows, and 0.5668 on OOV rows. The target-free dual-path system reaches Proposal Recall@16 0.6915 and end-to-end Exact@1 0.5212, compared with oracle conditional Exact@1 0.7450. On Mind2Web, the same audit yields SIR 0.2380 and an oracle-to-proposal gap of 0.2125. A 200-row semantic audit labels 0.7150 of exact-key OOV targets as semantically novel, 0.2450 as locator/string variation, and 0.0400 as ambiguous (Cohen's $\kappa=0.8173$). These measurements show why support composition must be controlled alongside candidate accuracy when offline results are used to reason about deployment.
entries.authors: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Daren Zha

entries.title: A domain-specific atomistic model for Earth's core materials
entries.abstract: Understanding Earth's core requires accurate descriptions of multicomponent iron alloys under extreme conditions. Here, we develop the Earth's Core Atomistic Model (ECAM) for Fe-Ni-S-Si-O-C-H alloys through sampling with a foundational atomistic model, targeted ab initio simulations, and iterative exploration. A compact dataset selected from nearly half a million configurations is consistently labeled using high-accuracy first-principles calculations and used to train a lightweight model. The model explicitly includes thermal electronic contributions and runs nearly two orders of magnitude faster than the original foundational model. ECAM corrects artifacts in the foundational model's description of core materials and reproduces the density, seismic velocity, Gibbs free energy, and phase diagrams of Fe and binary alloys in agreement with previous ab initio calculations. ECAM is expected to enable more realistic modeling of chemical partitioning and crystallization in Earth's core. Our workflow also provides a practical route from foundational-model sampling to efficient domain-specific simulation.
entries.authors: Tianqi Wan, Liangrui Wei, Zepeng Wu, Renata M. Wentzcovitch, Yang Sun

entries.title: Oscillations in two-stage contagion on networks: contagion structure, turnover and connectivity
entries.abstract: Two-stage contagion describes processes, such as the adoption of an opinion or of a technological novelty, in which an individual must be exposed to an adopter twice before adopting. With demographic turnover these processes can generate waves of adoption and abandonment. We study these oscillations in a two-stage contagion model with turnover through a reservoir of inactive individuals and a small rate of spontaneous activation, and report four main findings. (i) In the mean-field description the oscillations are born at a supercritical Hopf bifurcation and require a predominantly two-stage contagion (first-contact adoption probability $Q\lesssim0.17$) and a slow turnover; spontaneous activation acts as a perturbation that destroys them. (ii) In finite populations demographic noise sustains quasi-cycles also outside this region, with a spectrum and variance predicted by a linear noise approximation away from the Hopf bifurcation. (iii) Reducing the connectivity of the network damps the oscillation, because naive nodes see fewer active neighbours than in a well-mixed population, and correlations measured in simulations confirm this damping mechanism; a pair approximation predicts that the sustained cycle disappears below a critical mean degree $\kc$, which decreases as $Q$ and the turnover rate decrease, and a finite-size test with up to $3.2\times10^5$ nodes confirms this threshold in simulations. (iv) At low connectivity the amplitude no longer depends on $Q$, so that sparsity erases the signature of the two-stage mechanism, whereas a faster turnover reduces the relative amplitude at every connectivity. The irregular dynamics observed in simulations are noise-driven quasi-cycles, not chaos.
entries.authors: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no, Luca Meacci, Mario Primicerio

entries.title: Confoundry: Spatial Causal Discovery and Dynamic Effect Mapping from Earth Observation Time Series
entries.abstract: Earth observation time series provide extensive historical observations of environmental change, but causal relationships inferred from them may vary geographically and depend heavily on local model adequacy. We introduce Confoundry, a framework for spatially resolved causal discovery and dynamic effect estimation from heterogeneous Earth observation time series. Confoundry aligns multi-source raster data, removes deterministic seasonal and long-term variation, fits separate structural VAR--LiNGAM models at individual grid cells, and propagates bootstrap estimation uncertainty into mapped dynamic responses. Model diagnostics are evaluated spatially so that mapped responses can be restricted to locations meeting predefined model checks. We demonstrate the approach using monthly MODIS NDVI and ERA5-Land hydroclimatic variables over the Iberian Peninsula from 2005--2024. Of 27,050 fitted pixel models, 14,657 passed the primary diagnostic criteria. The retained models yield geographically heterogeneous model-implied NDVI responses to precipitation, temperature, potential evaporation, and shallow and deep soil moisture. Aggregated responses vary systematically along an external aridity gradient: water-related responses become relatively stronger toward drier environments, whereas temperature responses increase toward wetter conditions. A single-pixel synthetic benchmark illustrates substantial finite-record variation in recovered causal structure and dynamic effects from 20-year monthly time series. The results demonstrate that spatial causal mapping of Earth observation data is most informative when estimated responses, uncertainty, and local model adequacy are reported together.
entries.authors: Vytautas Jancauskas, Daniela Espinoza-Molina, Samuel Garske

entries.title: marineGeochemFoam: A multipurpose framework for simulating reactive transport and biogeochemical cycling in marine sediments and at seawater-groundwater interfaces
entries.abstract: We present marineGeochemFoam, an open-source reactive transport modeling framework for simulating early diagenesis, sediment burial, submarine groundwater discharge, and biogeochemical cycling in marine sediments and groundwater-seawater transition zones. The code is implemented in the widely used numerical toolbox OpenFOAM and extends the capabilities of the existing diagenetic models by supporting, among other features, i) coupled reactive transport of dissolved solute and solid species, (ii) a flexible native reaction package, supporting arbitrary reaction networks with n-th order and Monod-type kinetics, and (iii) coupling with an external geochemical code, PHREEEQC, providing access to a wide range of thermodynamically based geochemical processes. We benchmarked different features of the code across various examples with increasing complexity. Successively, the code was applied to two case studies reproducing field observations from the Hanko groundwater discharge site, Finland, and the Santa Barbara Basin, California. Beyond diagenetic applications, the code also serves as a general-purpose reactive transport simulator.
entries.authors: Navid Ahmadi, Evgenii Kortunov, Karim Norouzi Moghanjoghi, Joonas J. Virtasalo, Muhammad Muniruzzaman

entries.title: An ensemble of graph generative models for assisted history matching of the Brugge field case
entries.abstract: Assisted history matching remains non-unique because many geological realisations can reproduce equivalent production responses with substantial differences between individual well matches. This ambiguity increases when a field comprises several depositional settings and modelling strategies. The paper applied a graph autoencoder approach to history matching of a benchmark Brugge field that comprises different depositional zones. Each stratigraphic zone is modelled with its dedicated generative model that comprises a joint latent space for optimisation history matching loops. Graph-based generators operate directly on the active cells of the corner-point grid, so its irregular geometry is handled without conversion to a regular lattice. The optimisation search in the 160-dimensional joint latent space is done with the Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy. The multi-component objective function includes static well data mismatch, dynamic production mismatch, and a geological realism penalty based on the Decoder induced latent metric. Latent space diagnostics with topological data analysis are applied prior to history matching to test whether one generator is sufficient or whether a multiple generator formulation is required. The results show that the zone-based formulation gives coherent latent spaces, preserves the main porosity and permeability relations that vary from one zone to another, and supports history matching while keeping the solutions within the learned geological manifold. The matched models reproduce field oil and water production within the prior uncertainty range and provide a comparable well-level match to previously published Brugge studies based on Ensemble Kalman Filter, Particle Swarm Optimisation with principal component analysis of parameterisation, and Multiple Kernel Learning with Particle Swarm Optimisation.
entries.authors: Gleb Shishaev, Anton Shirokov, Shadfar Davoodi, Mohammed Al-Shargabi, Vasily Demyanov, Daniel Arnold

entries.title: Token Importance-Aware Semantic Communication Enabled Robust Video Transmission
entries.abstract: Video applications are increasingly prevalent, yet their high data volume and temporal dependency make robust wireless transmission challenging under limited communication resources. To address this issue, we propose a token importance-aware semantic communication (Ti-SemCom) framework for bandwidth-efficient video transmission. Specifically, object and motion information is jointly extracted to identify communication-relevant regions, which are hierarchically associated with semantic tokens according to their importance. The transmitted tokens are then dynamically selected based on both token importance and the available bandwidth, prioritizing more informative video content under resource constraints. At the receiver, untransmitted regions reuse recently reconstructed references to further reduce redundant transmission. Experiments on the CAVIAR dataset show that Ti-SemCom can achieve an 88.3\% reduction in communication cost while maintaining competitive reconstruction quality.
entries.authors: Xiwen Zhang, Yubo Peng, Luping Xiang, Kun Yang

entries.title: A novel derivative-corrected within-host viral model based on Caputo-Fabrizio fractional dynamics
entries.abstract: We study an implicit within-host viral dynamics model for uninfected target cells $H(t)$, infected cells $I(t)$, viral load $V(t)$, and damaged or removed cells $D(t)$. The model contains a parameter $\mathfrak{a}\in[0,1]$ that blends the classical instantaneous within-host dynamics with derivative-dependent correction terms. We rewrite the system as an explicit ordinary differential equation whenever a computable determinant $\Delta(H,V)$ is nonzero, derive sufficient conditions for local and global well-posedness, prove positivity and conservation of $H+I+D$, compute the basic reproduction number by the next-generation approach, and analyze long-time behavior. Under natural nondegeneracy assumptions, $I(t)\to0$, $V(t)\to0$, $H(t)\to H_\infty>0$, and $D(t)\to D_\infty$. We also derive peak conditions, a final-size identity, and discuss the biological interpretation of $\mathfrak{a}$ as a dynamical responsiveness or short-memory parameter.
entries.authors: Dora Sele\v{s}i, Danijela Rajter-\'Ciri\'c, N\'ora Juh\'asz, Gergely R\"ost

entries.title: Topology-Aware Reinforcement Learning for CAD Decomposition toward All-Hexahedral Meshing
entries.abstract: Automatic hexahedral meshing for complex CAD models has long been regarded as the "holy grail" of mesh generation. The fundamental challenge arises from feature misalignment, where orthogonal or interacting features coexist, making direct hexahedral meshing infeasible and requiring decomposition into simpler, meshable blocks. While existing decomposition methods, including frame-field pipelines and learning-based techniques, have reduced manual intervention, they can remain sensitive to geometric and topological complexity and may fail to produce valid decompositions for challenging feature configurations. Specifically, their action spaces are typically restricted to surface-based splitting, which often yields invalid or unmeshable decompositions. To address these limitations, we propose DecompRL, a deep reinforcement learning framework for CAD decomposition toward hexahedral meshing. We design a set of topology-aware internal-splitting actions that leverage both global topological structure and local geometric property to effectively separate misaligned features. Furthermore, we introduce geometric rewards together with meshability feedback to guide the learning process toward valid decompositions and high-quality meshes. Extensive experiments on ABC, Fusion360, NIST, and DeepCAD show that DecompRL achieves the highest success rate among the evaluated learning-based methods on three of the four benchmarks, while maintaining competitive mesh quality. The measured LMFF-to-DecompRL runtime ratio reaches up to two orders of magnitude; this compares the full LMFF procedure with DecompRL decomposition alone, excluding subsequent mesh generation. The largest SR improvement is observed on Fusion360, where DecompRL reaches a success rate of 59.6%.
entries.authors: Jiaming Peng, Zhihao Zheng, Rui Wang, Qinglin Wang, Jing Xiao, Jie Liu, Na Lei, Xinhai Chen

entries.title: Geometric Hammocks: Surface Laminations and the Ziegler Spectrum of String Algebras
entries.abstract: We give the first complete topological, geometric, and ergodic classification of the Ziegler spectrum $\Zg(\Lambda)$ of a non-domestic string algebra $\Lambda$ over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary cardinality, via a dictionary with Thurston's theory of geodesic laminations on a cusped hyperbolic surface. This is a model-theoretic counterpart of Haiden--Katzarkov--Kontsevich's realization (\emph{Publ.\ Math.\ IHES} 2017) of stability conditions on the bounded derived category of a gentle algebra via flat surfaces: pure-injective modules correspond to admissible geodesics, and the Ziegler topology to a corridor quotient of Chabauty space. Three consequences follow. The Krull--Gabriel dimension equals the surface's topological accumulation depth, and the string closure with all higher Cantor--Bendixson strata is globally homeomorphic to an explicit corridor space, with the pushout map to $\Zg(\Lambda)$ a homeomorphism if and only if $\Lambda$ is domestic. Prefix-free dyadic blocks in the geometric perfect core verify Puninski's cardinality-free two-chain criterion, resolving the open problem of superdecomposable pure-injectives over uncountable fields for all non-domestic string and special biserial algebras. Three purely algebraic invariants on the perfect core---localized pp-shape entropy, a $K_0$-weighted pressure function satisfying an algebraic Ruelle--Walters Variational Principle, and a pp-bifurcation index with a Gauss--Bonnet simplicity obstruction---strictly separate uncountable iso-entropic and iso-pressure families, and the inverse limit of the quotient pp-lattice recovers the transversal Cantor cross-section.
entries.authors: Shantanu Sardar

entries.title: Auditable Human-Agent Teams for Autonomous X-ray Experimentation
entries.abstract: Closed-loop autonomous experimentation can accelerate scientific discovery, but implementation effort limits accessibility. Agentic systems may lower this barrier, although sustained operation on physical instruments remains largely unexplored. Here, using coding-agent infrastructure grounded in validated scientific methods, we demonstrate autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices under evolving, human-defined objectives. Complete human-agent and agent-agent transcripts enable an audit that reconstructs decision provenance and characterizes the division of cognitive labor. Across three experiments, 61-67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while the share of methodological and scientific contributions increased from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56-61% in later experiments. Provenance showed that 59-68% of error corrections involved multiple participants and that about half of all decisions incorporated the input of another participant. These results may guide design principles for multi-agent scientific systems and inform future agent harnesses, model training, and accessible autonomous experimentation.
entries.authors: Gunik Luthra, Ronald J. Pandolfi, Benjamin T. Diroll, Ricky Ronquillo, Ruipeng Li, Christopher B. Murray, Marcus M. Noack, Kevin G. Yager, Esther H. R. Tsai

entries.title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
entries.abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. We introduce EarthRecord, a benchmark built on the raw record of 56 sites: four decades of Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS, and Sentinel-2 data, with cloud masking and cross-sensor harmonization left to the agent. It poses 238 land-change questions across ten analysis tasks, scored against withheld references from global products, agreement among methods, and visual interpretation. Two controls test what answers rest on: the closed book removes the record, and instrument pairs alter one satellite's data while nothing changes on the ground. Evaluations of twelve multimodal agents reveal that leading agents complete most analyses end to end but falter when an answer requires mapping from imagery. Further analysis shows that the record moves answers from prior knowledge to the pixels but not yet to the real change on the ground: when one satellite's data are altered, half of the right answers follow the alteration. EarthRecord thus provides a principled platform for measuring and advancing agents from pixels to land change.
entries.authors: Haoran Zhang, Huizhen Sun, Hanbin Wen, Jie Leng, Jiaxin Zhu, Zhaohua Sun

entries.title: Train on prefill, monitor at decode: Using sparse autoencoders for topic monitoring
entries.abstract: Topic monitoring is the task of labelling the topic of each token in a model's response during generation. Activation-based monitors that run at generation time have so far been trained to detect harmful content and are limited to two or three classes. We introduce TopicScope, a framework for training causal topic classifiers on SAE features that assign a topic to every token, so that the label can change partway through a response. We train three detector architectures on synthetic multi-topic conversations covering seven topics. Across Gemma-3 1B and 4B, monitors trained on features extracted from prefill hidden states were able to generalise to decoding. We also found that the classifiers are robust to perturbations, losing at most 5 macro-F1 points when off-topic asides are inserted, topics are removed or sections are reordered. Ablations conducted to understand the contribution of the SAE revealed that classifiers reaching baseline performance without it were several times larger. Our findings show that compact topic monitors can be trained inexpensively in prefill and deployed during generation. More broadly, our work shows where SAEs are useful beyond safety classification. Our code, dataset and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/Mercity-AI/SAE-Guardrails and https://huggingface.co/collections/Mercity/online-guardrails-using-sparse-autoencoders-6ac602940468c62fefb2b9e8
entries.authors: Rishikesh Mallagundla, Pranav Patel

entries.title: LandslideFM: A Foundation Model Towards Unified Landslide Perception and Understanding
entries.abstract: Intelligent landslide detection is essential for disaster prevention. However, existing models primarily focus on isolated visual tasks, require extensive labeled data, and lack deep analytical and scene-understanding capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose LandslideFM, the first unified foundation model that connects visual perception tasks with contextual interpretation of landslides. Specifically, LandslideFM adapts to multiple visual tasks via a Source-Agreement Graduated Trust semi-supervised learning framework that leverages limited labeled data alongside abundant unlabeled data. Furthermore, predicted landslide regions provide explicit spatial guidance to a Vision-Language Model adapted through parameter-efficient fine-tuning, enabling comprehensive landslide reasoning. To support training and evaluation in this domain, we also present LandslideVL, the first benchmark for intelligent landslide analysis, combining visual imagery and newly introduced textual prompts. Comprehensive experiments across public datasets and LandslideVL demonstrate that LandslideFM achieves superior quantitative and qualitative performance. Most importantly, LandslideFM surpasses general-purpose VLMs in specialized landslide reasoning and scene analysis. Our code is released at https://github.com/wangshanwen001/LandslideFM.
entries.authors: Shanwen Wang, Sirui Wang, Xin Sun, Jungong Han

entries.title: Tracing Psychometric Inference in Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Do large language models represent psychological constructs internally, or do they only generate outputs that resemble psychometric structure? We address this question using a cross-persona paradigm across 14 model variants from two families (Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5, 0.5B-14B, base and instruct). Given responses on one psychological scale from real individuals (N = 272 Taiwanese university students), models predict responses on six other scales. At the behavioral level, larger variants reproduce and amplify human cross-scale correlations; amplification persists after correcting the seven-scale human correlations for measurement attenuation. We then examine whether this structure is reflected internally. Contrastive direction analysis finds geometry aligned with the human matrix in larger instruct variants, but little alignment in base variants under this assay. Across models, geometry strength is associated with behavioral amplification (r = 0.68, p = 0.008; partial r = 0.69 controlling for log size). To relate internal structure to output behavior, a matched activation-probing paradigm shows that probe slopes vary less than behavioral slopes (1.38-1.77 vs 0.52-1.53). A synthetic control shows that ridge probing can inflate these slopes; after subtracting a baseline based on a reliability proxy from another analysis, adjusted slopes remain associated with behavior (r = 0.88). We term the measured probe-behavior gap readout attenuation. These results establish decodability and geometric alignment under the tested assays, without showing that the measured directions mediate the cross-persona answers.
entries.authors: Chih-Hao Hsu, Feng-Chun B. Chou, Pin-Hao A. Chen

entries.title: Graph Visualizations in Prompts for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
entries.abstract: We study when and how multimodal input improves knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) in large vision--language models. Using a controlled evaluation over 1,500 WebQSP and CWQ questions and six VLMs within a fixed KGQA pipeline, we compare text-only prompting against text-plus-graph visualization at the per-question level and analyze performance changes as a function of reasoning complexity, model size, and image layout. Adding a graph image yields an average gain of 1.85 F1 points, driven by strong precision improvements on low-complexity questions (+4.65 F1). Mixed-effects and regression analyses show that these multimodal gains do not depend strongly on model scale, but are highly sensitive to graph layout: image-only settings sharply degrade performance, hierarchical Graphviz layouts outperform less organized renderings, and decomposing large subgraphs into separated paths yields the largest improvements. Taken together, the results indicate that visual prompting primarily aids KGQA by enhancing prediction precision in low-complexity contexts, provided that visual design respects cognitive and perceptual constraints. To optimize both accuracy and inference efficiency, we argue for adaptive visual prompting policies that selectively append diagrams to small, visually sparse subgraphs with well-structured layouts, avoiding unnecessary visual clutter and token overhead on complex queries. We conclude by relating these findings to a visual notation design theory, outlining how principled diagram encoding can guide future multimodal VLM prompting.
entries.authors: Luiz do Valle Miranda, Andreas L. Opdahl, Grzegorz J. Nalepa

entries.title: Reinforcement Learning based control of Cancer Chemotherapy treatments
entries.abstract:
Reinforcement Learning has achieved tremendous success in recent years. Extending its scope from the traditional complex games such as Atari, Go, Pokeman, and Chess, reinforcement learning has caught researchers' attention on modelling real-life scenarios. Personalized medicine and the dynamic treatment regimen are two such preliminary research fields; researchers are focusing their mindsets currently. Estimating the optimal dynamic treatment regimens from the observational real clinical data is being popularized among the researchers, widening its scope towards more advanced versions of reinforcement learning algorithms.
  This research is about a research study that focused on reinforcement learning techniques that have been approached in the context of cancer chemotherapy treatments. Primarily this thesis addresses the result of the study by means of the state-of-the-art on reinforcement learning techniques used in generating the optimal policy for sequential treatments, including the existing online reinforcement learning approaches. Thereby a simulation for cancer chemotherapy via traditional Q-learning would be presented. Secondly, the study will extend towards using offline reinforcement learning in the optimal policy generation. Thus, the proposed solution follows a data-driven approach, which works on the real human colon cancer clinical data.
  The novelty of the proposed solution resides in the implementation of an offline reinforcement learning approach by means of a model-based architecture using the conservative Q-learning and the model-based offline policy optimization algorithm. As per the experimental results and the evaluations, it was revealed that the proposed Chemo RL model caters well the problem of cancer chemotherapy treatment scheduling and serves as a supportive model for the junior oncologists in deciding their treatment decisions.
entries.authors: Jayakody Kankanamalage Chamani Shiranthika

entries.title: AI Governance Should Prioritize Control and Knowledge Boundaries Over Limiting Intelligence
entries.abstract: The rapid proliferation of autonomously acting AI agents makes the governance of agentic systems urgent. We propose the competence circuit, summarized as IKC + KC + C, that decomposes an agent's real-world impact into three pathways: intelligence-mediated discovery, procedural know-how, and direct control. Using the canonical fast-takeoff debate as a stress test, we formalize the conditions for intelligence-mediated fast takeoff as a conjunction jointly sufficient for fast catastrophic supremacy, showing that most rely on rapid knowledge acquisition or control attainment rather than intelligence alone. We operationalize epistemic intelligence as hypothesis-selection efficiency and validate this framework via stochastic simulation on NK fitness landscapes across six scenarios spanning the conjunctive chain. An analytic bound supported by the simulations shows that intelligence-driven speedup is capped by the ratio of competing intelligence levels regardless of task difficulty. The simulations also expose a fast-takeoff dilemma: a large intelligence-driven speedup multiplier materializes only when the hypothesis space is noisy, but the absolute timescale remains constrained by the time required for capability-critical tests, so a large multiplier need not imply rapid progress. Simulations also indicate that institutional chokepoints disproportionately slow down superintelligent agents when mandatory authorization delays are large relative to the negligible time these agents spend on unproductive search. We argue that the dominant safety levers are restricting control and enforcing knowledge boundaries rather than limiting intelligence alone, and this applies to agentic systems at any capability level. Purely digital domains weaken these bottlenecks, strengthening the case for architectures that intentionally "put physics in the loop."
entries.authors: Hendrik Luuk

entries.title: Tabular Foundation Models vs Tuned Gradient Boosting for Telecom Churn: A Profit- and Calibration-Aware Evaluation
entries.abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) predict from a labelled context in a single forward pass. A recent benchmark reported that they decisively outperform tree ensembles for customer churn, but it compared them with untuned gradient-boosted trees (GBDTs) and scored only ranking metrics, while a retention campaign is judged in money. We re-evaluate TabPFN-2.5, TabPFN-3.5, TabPFN-3.5-Fast and TabICL v2 against Optuna-tuned GBDTs on five public telecom churn datasets over 10 seeded splits. We separate three questions: whether a model ranks churners well, whether that ranking earns more expected maximum profit (EMP), and whether its probabilities can drive a threshold policy. With a split-aware test and Holm correction over 20 pre-declared comparisons, TabPFN-3.5 earns significantly more EMP than the best tuned GBDT on Cell2Cell (1.9%) and Iranian (7.6%), and these two gains also hold against each of the three tuned GBDTs separately. On Orange it is ahead in all 10 splits (14.3%), but the gain is not significant after correction (Holm p = 0.155). The splits resample the same datasets, so these results do not stand for independent operators. TabICL v2, the earlier benchmark's leader, beats the best tuned GBDT only on Iranian, not all three of them, and underpredicts Orange churn by 2.1 points on a 7.3% base rate. On the datasets and splits where we tested them, a substantially larger tuning budget and a duplicate-aware split leave the main conclusions unchanged. Retuning the baseline cuts the earlier headline gap from 6.1 to 4.0 PR-AUC points without closing it. The licence of the TabPFN-3.5 weights we used (License v1.0), not scoring cost, is what stands between its gains and production use.
entries.authors: Ismail Hossain Polas

entries.title: When Proofs Are Abundant, What Is a Paper For?
entries.abstract: AI systems now produce formally verified proofs of celebrated open problems, and the cost of obtaining a correct proof is falling toward zero. If correctness becomes cheap, what is left for a research paper to communicate? I argue that a paper is not exhausted by a verified statement. It is a narrative exposed to the criticism of a community, made of an intension (the author's choice of problem and perspective), a scientific chain of thought (the reasoning steps leading to the result), and the arguments supporting each step. Most published mathematics is judged on these two elements rather than on correctness alone, and machine-generated formal scripts convey neither. Borrowing from logic and type theory, I formalise the first as a Derivation-Level Intension and the second as a Directional Extension: a decomposition of a proof into cut-points whose axiomatic footprints reveal its weak links, where the result could be strengthened, and its strong links, which can be transported to other theories. Moreover, I examine five roles AI can play in the research process, including bibliographical search and critical judgment, and show that none of them removes the need to declare these two elements. I mention ways these two concepts could be useful for Journals and for training of young mathematicians in a AI era. If proofs become abundant, the scarce resource is not correctness but a community's shared understanding of why a result matters and how it could be pushed further.
entries.authors: Charles-Albert Lehalle

entries.title: SetPrint: Black-Box LLM Fingerprinting via Setwise Correspondence of Response Changes
entries.abstract: Black-box LLM fingerprinting aims to determine whether a target model was derived from a source model when only the output responses to input queries are observable. One way to reveal this relationship is to perturb each query and observe the resulting responses of both models, yielding two corresponding sets of response variations. These sets provide two complementary sources of information: the relations among response changes within each set, and the correspondence of response changes between the two sets. Existing approaches, however, have not fully exploited both. We introduce \textbf{SetPrint}, a training-free method that jointly captures both within-set relations and between-set correspondence. SetPrint expresses each response change relative to the mean change of its own set, and then compares changes from the two models that were induced by the same perturbation. On LeaFBench, SetPrint consistently outperforms existing training-free black-box fingerprinting methods. Further analyses attribute these gains to both within-set relations and between-set correspondence.
